cand.title: 28th Enhanced Safety of Vehicles (ESV) Conference
cand.organizationName: Transport Canada and the international Enhanced Safety of Vehicles community
cand.excerpt: Four-day international technical conference in Toronto combining technical sessions, live demonstrations, exhibits, student competition, networking, and technical tours involving government, industry, academia, and international participants.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Verified organizing contacts, not proven hotel-contract signatories: Zuzanna Strom, ESV Committee Secretariat Lead and Manager, Road Users and Consumer Awareness; Michelle Rozon, ESV Committee Secretariat Deputy Lead and Senior Program Officer, Road Users and Consumer Awareness; David Woods, ESV Exhibition Coordinator and Policy Analyst, Road Users and Consumer Awareness, Transport Canada. Strom and Rozon are the strongest organizing/access-routing leads; Woods is relevant to exhibitor and associated delegation logistics. Accommodation procurement authority is unverified for all three.
findings.futureEdition: The 28th ESV took place May 12–15, 2026; registration, setup, a workshop and technical tours also occurred on May 11. It is past as of November 15, 2026 and outside the December 2026–June 2028 horizon. No officially published next-edition dates or city were located. Do not promote a third-party 29th ESV 2028/TBD listing as an announcement. The series is officially described as biennial, but the actual 2019–2023–2026 intervals do not support extrapolating a date.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: a city-hotel satellite lodging role is more realistic than a resort programme or whole-conference bid. A March 2026 official presentation described approximately 1,000 participants, a pre-event estimate rather than verified actual attendance. Radisson Blu’s supplied 157-room inventory and approximately 240-theatre largest room cannot accommodate that entire programme. A future Toronto edition could potentially support a modest delegate, speaker, exhibitor or VIP sub-block, or small side meetings; 15–109 peak rooms is a hotel sales-target range, NOT published ESV demand. The event was at Exhibition Place, so MTCC walkability is not an event-specific advantage. No travel-time or shuttle claim is established. Catering/restaurant operation remains unverified; do not promise catered receptions.
findings.venueCommitments: Historical 2026 venue: Exhibition Place, 100 Princes’ Blvd, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, within Toronto proper and the hotel’s Exhibition Place territory, not the MTCC. Enercare Centre housed exhibits and the May 12 welcome reception in Hall C; the Automotive Building housed plenary and technical sessions. The May 14 gala was at 360 Restaurant at the CN Tower, 290 Bremner Blvd. These are past edition commitments, not future available business. No next-edition venue verified.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified recent timeline: 25th, June 5–8, 2017, Detroit, Michigan, United States (exact building not verified); 26th, June 10–13, 2019, Evoluon, Eindhoven, Netherlands; 27th, April 3–6, 2023, Pacifico Yokohama North, Yokohama, Japan; 28th, May 12–15, 2026, Exhibition Place, Toronto, Canada. Transport Canada describes member-country hosting alternating between North America, Europe and Asia. This is an internationally rotating government conference, not a verified recurring Toronto account.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Edition-specific organizer-arranged courtesy rates with attendee booking links, not a verified exclusive housing bureau or guaranteed room allotment. Exact official quote: “We’ve partnered with select hotels to offer courtesy rates for conference attendees. We recommend booking early, as rooms will fill quickly and there is limited space. The web link under each hotel provides a link to the courtesy rate available.” All named courtesy-rate properties: Chelsea Hotel; Courtyard Marriott Toronto; InterContinental Toronto Centre; Hyatt Regency; Delta Hotels Toronto Airport & Conference Centre; Embassy Suites by Hilton Toronto Airport; Four Points by Sheraton Toronto Airport; Element Toronto Airport; Holiday Inn Toronto International Airport. Four Points and Element appear together in one listing. Hotel X is separately identified on the venue map as onsite accommodation; no Hotel X courtesy-rate or exclusive host-hotel contract is established by that reference. Destination Toronto’s general city-centre directory is an additional referral, not an edition-specific booking commitment. No public room-allotment counts, pickup, room nights, housing-bureau mandate or open hotel RFP were located.
findings.organizationStructure: Public-sector international technical programme co-hosted in 2026 by Transport Canada and the U.S. Department of Transportation’s NHTSA, not a membership association or corporate trade-show owner. Participating governments determine the conference venue. D.E. Systems’ MyConferenceSuite is evidenced as the registration-system provider, not as an appointed housing bureau, DMC or full-service PCO. No wider PCO appointment verified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Historical 2026 competition included nine named courtesy-rate properties and separately Hotel X onsite. Radisson Blu was not listed. This establishes competing accommodation pathways, not exclusive allocation of all demand. The organizer’s warning of limited space is not proof of sellout, unmet overflow or displaced room nights. No quantified overflow or room pickup was found. Gala and welcome reception already had named historical venues.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Do not issue a dated group quote or forecast room nights. Ask the published ESV organizing channel to route an introduction to Zuzanna Strom or Michelle Rozon; use David Woods for exhibitor-delegation routing. Seek a post-event debrief on courtesy-rate uptake and whether any Toronto follow-on meetings are planned, then ask who selects hotels and whether/how additional properties can participate. Present a nonexclusive small-block capability only if a future Toronto need is confirmed. Verify hotel food-and-beverage availability before offering catered side events.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Closed as a current sales opportunity: the Toronto edition finished May 15, 2026. The registration endpoint is now titled Closed. Historical courtesy-rate links do not establish live inventory or an open procurement process. No confirmed event-led lodging opportunity in Toronto during December 2026–June 2028 was located.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional relationship development only, not qualified future Toronto room demand. Government-led international rotation limits capture by this Toronto hotel. First establish whether any next edition or related organizer/delegation meeting will actually be in Toronto, then identify the accommodation decision-maker and timing. Do not assume a 2028 date or Toronto return from biennial language.
